Can I ask, how is is supposed to be working in the grand scheme of things?

For example pldm daemon has discovered a SmartNIC which reports via its PLDM PDR 3 Redfish Resources with `"ContainingResourceID": 0` (EXTERNAL):
1)
```
"ProposedContainingResourceName": "NetworkAdapterCollection.NetworkAdapterCollection"
"MajorSchemaName": "NetworkAdapter.NetworkAdapter"
```
2)
```
"ProposedContainingResourceName": "PCIeDeviceCollection.PCIeDeviceCollection"
"MajorSchemaName": "PCIeDevice.PCIeDevice"
```
3)
```
"ProposedContainingResourceName": "NetworkInterfaceCollection.NetworkInterfaceCollection"
"MajorSchemaName": "NetworkInterface.NetworkInterface"
```

How will PLDM daemon know which absolute URLs correspond to these resources?

By design this is not resolved here in libbej — this patch only
  performs the DSP0218 Table 42 placeholder <-> value substitution against a
  caller-supplied BejDeferredBindingMap. Deciding the absolute URLs is the
  consumer's (pldmd's) responsibility, and it is not arbitrary: pldmd follows the
  Redfish spec, encoded as a static collection-URI table.

  On the pldmd side the flow is:

  1. The Redfish Resource PDRs are parsed into per-resource metadata
     (resourceId, ProposedContainingResourceName, MajorSchemaName,
     ContainingResourceID, resource flags).
  2. pldmd maps each resource to its canonical Redfish collection via a static
     table derived from the Redfish schema/collection-URI conventions
     (e.g. NetworkAdapterCollection -> /redfish/v1/Chassis/<ns>/NetworkAdapters).
     It then builds the map entry: uri (for %L<id>), instanceId (for %I<id>),
     and action targets (for %T<id>.<action>). The final URI is
     <collection-prefix>/<instanceId>.
  3. That map is passed to decode()/encode().

  For ContainingResourceID = 0 (EXTERNAL), pldmd does not rely on the device's
  proposed position; it places the resource under the spec-defined collection
  keyed by ProposedContainingResourceName / MajorSchemaName. So for your SmartNIC
  example (tid = T, resourceId = R) these resolve to:

  - NetworkAdapterCollection / NetworkAdapter
      -> /redfish/v1/Chassis/<ns>/NetworkAdapters/<instanceId>
  - PCIeDeviceCollection / PCIeDevice
      -> /redfish/v1/Systems/<ns>/PCIeDevices/<instanceId>
  - NetworkInterfaceCollection / NetworkInterface
      -> /redfish/v1/Systems/<ns>/NetworkInterfaces/<instanceId>

  Note: the <ns> namespace segment (e.g. "RDE") and the <instanceId> form
  (e.g. RDE_<tid>_<resourceId>) are pldmd implementation choices and can be
  changed by the implementation; libbej just substitutes the placeholders with those values.
Do you have open-source implementation of pldmd patches for this functionality?

I think earlier you've asked is libbej a correct place for placeholder substitution.

I've read RDE specification more thoroughly and indeed looks like the best place for such kind of substitution is libbej:

> DSP0218_1.2.0
> 8.3 Deferred binding of data 

> All substitution macros are bracketed with the percent sign (%) character. 
While it would in theory be possible for the MC to check every string it decodes for the presence of this escape character, in practice that would be an inefficient waste of MC processing time. Instead, the RDE Device shall flag any string containing substitution macros with the deferred binding bit set to inform the MC of their presence; the MC shall only perform macro substitution if the deferred binding bit is set.

> Defaults to empty, which leaves placeholders / raw %L<id> in the output.

I'm not sure of the actual benefit, but specification requires to translate placeholders without bindings too:

> % L<resource-ID> 

> The MC-assigned URI of an RDE Provider defined resource (specified by a
> resource ID within the target PDR), or /invalid.PDR<resource-ID> if
> unrecognized resource ID

So it looks like if we don't have mapping for resource id 123 for example, we need to translate it from `%L123` to `/invalid.PDR123`

For the default (empty map) 

I'd like to keep the current passthrough
the raw string is left untouched as an explicit "resolution disabled" mode for callers.

Decode without supplying bindings, and document the two modes (empty =
disabled/passthrough; non-empty = resolve, unknown id -> /invalid.PDR<XX> form).

Substitution is already gated on the per-string deferred-binding bit, so ordinary
data is unaffected either way.
DSP0218 Table 42 has many other markers. Please note in the commit message which markers are currently supported with this change

reworked the data model in this revision.

BejDeferredBindingMap is no
longer keyed by resource id with a per-resource struct. It is now a flat map keyed
by the placeholder token (the text after '%'), value = substitution

using BejDeferredBindingMap = std::unordered_map<std::string, std::string>;

Id-less markers are first-class -- %C/%S are just tokens "C"/"S", no resource id,
no empty fields:

bindings[bejBinding::resourceLink(30)] = "/redfish/v1/.../Drives/1"; // %L30
bindings[bejBinding::instanceId(30)] = "1"; // %I30
bindings[bejBinding::action(30, 1)] = ".../Actions/Drive.Reset"; // %T30.1
bindings[bejBinding::chassis()] = "/redfish/v1/Chassis/1U"; // %C
bindings[bejBinding::system()] = "/redfish/v1/Systems/1"; // %S

